picks.headline: Rare-variant genetic architecture of height in over 1.4 million individuals
picks.blurb: Exome data from over 1.4 million people implicate 207 genes in height, including rare loss-of-function variants with effects far larger than typical common variants.

picks.headline: Single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map for coronary artery disease
picks.blurb: Profiling gene activity and chromatin in coronary arteries from 44 people links non-coding disease variants to specific cell types and gene programmes, including smooth muscle cells.

picks.headline: Pharming pauses Ruconest production over fill-finish issue, threatening US supply
picks.blurb: A third-party manufacturer's problem led the drugmaker to halt output of its core product and caution that shortages are likely.

picks.headline: Buckle up: Opdivo biosimilar settlement sets BMS up for make-or-break moment
picks.blurb: Under the Amgen and Bristol Myers Squibb settlement, a biosimilar version of the PD-1 drug Opdivo can reach the market in 2028.

picks.headline: Washington and Beijing are building walls around biotechnology. That's the wrong approach
picks.blurb: An opinion piece argues that restricting investment won't help the U.S. in contests it's already losing, and that eroding the research base is the bigger risk.

picks.headline: Senescence-targeting nanoparticles may enhance immunotherapy
picks.blurb: In mice, a nanoparticle treatment cleared the aging-related cells that drive tissue scarring around tumors, an early step toward improving how cancer immunotherapy works.

picks.headline: FDA approves Cogent's drug for rare stomach cancer
picks.blurb: The agency cleared the Cogent therapy for use alongside Pfizer's much older medicine Sutent.

picks.headline: Leqembi slows progression in Alzheimer's patients with Lewy bodies
picks.blurb: Analyses of the lecanemab Clarity trial and its five-year extension, presented at CTAD, suggest similar relative benefit with or without Lewy body pathology, though disease-modification claims remain debated.

picks.headline: Biomarker reckoning: Why did posdinemab take down p-tau, but not AD?
picks.blurb: Trial data shown at CTAD indicate the anti-tau antibody cut soluble p-tau217 in spinal fluid yet did not slow tangle spread or decline, prompting a closer look at biomarker meaning.

picks.headline: Medicare sets 2028 prices for 13 new drugs under Biden-era law
picks.blurb: CMS announced maximum prices for a third round of high-spend drugs, including Trulicity, Orencia and Cosentyx, widening Inflation Reduction Act cost controls to more older medicines.

picks.headline: Clinical landscape of cardiometabolic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
picks.blurb: A review frames this form of heart failure, increasingly tied to obesity and type 2 diabetes, as a mechanistic subtype involving endothelial dysfunction and metabolic inflexibility.

picks.headline: Sanofi's $41B Insmed buy, Capricor's second rejection, FDA's pre-holiday rush
picks.blurb: Sanofi's deal is the largest biopharma buyout since Pfizer's 2023 Seagen purchase, while the FDA again declined Capricor's Duchenne cell therapy and cleared several other companies' products.

picks.headline: Fertility advance: Engineered protein stabilizes chromosomes in aging eggs
picks.blurb: Mouse experiments suggest a lab-made protein complex can hold sister chromatids together as eggs age, a preclinical lead that could inform future IVF research.
